# Oska

> A secure-by-default language.

Oska 0.1.0 (pre-alpha). These docs track `main`. Every page is also served as Markdown: the same path with `.md`. Most of them are in [llms-full.txt](https://oskalang.dev/llms-full.txt), which leaves out the research, which is proposals and not documented behaviour (all in [llms-research.txt](https://oskalang.dev/llms-research.txt)). The source code is at https://github.com/aparsons/oska. A program is one `.osk` file or a package: an `oska.toml` and modules under `src/`, with `src/main.osk` as the entry and `use pkg.a.b` importing `src/a/b.osk`; see [Packages and modules](https://oskalang.dev/guide/packages.md). `oskac build` compiles a program to an executable for Linux or macOS on any host: `--target` picks the platform (`linux-aarch64`, `linux-x86_64`, `macos-aarch64` or `macos-x86_64`), `--target all` writes all four, and without `--target` it builds for the host. On Linux and macOS, `oskac run` and `oskac test` compile natively and run the executable, and `--interpret` selects the interpreter, which Windows uses; output, reports and exit codes are the same on both. See [Platform support](https://oskalang.dev/guide/cli-reference.md#platform-support).

## Docs

- [Oska](https://oskalang.dev/index.md): A secure-by-default language.
- [Glossary](https://oskalang.dev/glossary.md): Terms of the security model.
- [Oska design notes](https://oskalang.dev/design.md): Decisions are in adr/, terms in GLOSSARY.md, and the background in the research.
- [Reference](https://oskalang.dev/reference.md): How Oska works inside, the words it uses, and the decisions and research behind it. To use Oska, start with the guides.

## Decisions

- [Value semantics](https://oskalang.dev/adr/0001-values.md): Values are copied, not shared.
- [Capabilities are the effect system](https://oskalang.dev/adr/0002-capabilities.md): A function's capability parameters are its effects. See the design notes and ADR 0001.
- [Decisions](https://oskalang.dev/adr/index.md)

## Machine-readable

- [llms-full.txt](https://oskalang.dev/llms-full.txt): the documentation, as Markdown, in one file; it leaves out the research, which is proposals and not documented behaviour (all in [llms-research.txt](https://oskalang.dev/llms-research.txt))
- [search.json](https://oskalang.dev/search.json): the search index
- [sitemap.xml](https://oskalang.dev/sitemap.xml): the canonical URL of every page
- [latest.json](https://oskalang.dev/latest.json): the current version and the installers

## Optional

Internals most programs do not need, and research: proposals and background, not documented behaviour. Skip them unless you need them.

- [Oska runtime](https://oskalang.dev/runtime.md): See the checker, which is not in this tree.
- [Research: a report](https://oskalang.dev/research/2026-11-report.md): Proposal: Memory safety is the baseline (CISA).
- [llms-research.txt](https://oskalang.dev/llms-research.txt): every research page, as Markdown, in one file; proposals, not documented behaviour
